title.en: Cut an image into patch tokens
title.es: Corta una imagen en tokens de parche

prompt.en:
Write `patchify(image, p)` for an array of shape `(H, W, C)`. Cut it into `p x p` patches, ordered left to right and then top to bottom, and flatten each patch row by row (all channels of a pixel together). Return an array of shape `(number_of_patches, p * p * C)`.

Raise `ValueError` if `H` or `W` is not a multiple of `p`.
prompt.es:
Escribe `patchify(image, p)` para un array de forma `(H, W, C)`. Córtalo en parches de `p x p`, ordenados de izquierda a derecha y luego de arriba abajo, y aplana cada parche fila a fila (todos los canales de un píxel juntos). Devuelve un array de forma `(número_de_parches, p * p * C)`.

Lanza `ValueError` si `H` o `W` no son múltiplos de `p`.

tests:
import numpy as np
img = np.arange(4 * 6 * 3).reshape(4, 6, 3)
patches = patchify(img, 2)
assert patches.shape == (6, 12), "a 4 x 6 image with 2 x 2 patches gives 2 * 3 = 6 patches of 2 * 2 * 3 = 12 numbers"
assert np.array_equal(patches[0], img[0:2, 0:2].reshape(-1)), "patch 0 is the top-left square, flattened row by row"
assert np.array_equal(patches[1], img[0:2, 2:4].reshape(-1)), "patches go left to right first"
assert np.array_equal(patches[3], img[2:4, 0:2].reshape(-1)), "then top to bottom"
assert patchify(np.zeros((224, 224, 3)), 16).shape == (196, 768), "ViT: a 224 x 224 RGB image with 16 x 16 patches is 196 tokens of 768 numbers"
raised = False
try:
    patchify(np.zeros((5, 6, 3)), 2)
except ValueError:
    raised = True
assert raised, "a height that is not a multiple of p: raise ValueError"

hint.en: Reshape to `(H // p, p, W // p, p, C)`, swap the two middle axes with `transpose(0, 2, 1, 3, 4)`, then reshape to `(-1, p * p * C)`. Two nested loops over the grid work too.
hint.es: Cambia la forma a `(H // p, p, W // p, p, C)`, intercambia los dos ejes centrales con `transpose(0, 2, 1, 3, 4)` y vuelve a cambiarla a `(-1, p * p * C)`. Dos bucles anidados sobre la cuadrícula también sirven.

title.es: Los tokens de imagen crecen con la resolución

prompt.en: Write `patch_count(height, width, p)` that returns how many patch tokens an image produces when sides that are not a multiple of `p` are padded up to the next multiple. Then look at what doubling the resolution does.
prompt.es: Escribe `patch_count(height, width, p)`, que devuelve cuántos tokens de parche produce una imagen cuando los lados que no son múltiplos de `p` se rellenan hasta el siguiente múltiplo. Después observa qué ocurre al duplicar la resolución.

starter:
def patch_count(height, width, p):
    raise NotImplementedError
tests:
assert patch_count(224, 224, 16) == 196, "224 / 16 = 14, and 14 x 14 = 196"
assert patch_count(1344, 1344, 16) == 36 * 196, "six times the side gives 36 times the patches"
assert patch_count(448, 224, 16) == 392, "a 2:1 image has twice the patches"
assert patch_count(230, 224, 16) == 15 * 14, "230 pixels need 15 rows of patches once padded"
assert patch_count(1, 1, 14) == 1, "even a tiny image is one patch"
assert patch_count(448, 448, 16) ** 2 == 16 * patch_count(224, 224, 16) ** 2, "doubling the side quadruples the tokens and multiplies attention cost by 16"

hint.en: Integer ceiling division: `-(-height // p)`. Multiply the rows by the columns.
hint.es: División entera redondeando hacia arriba: `-(-height // p)`. Multiplica filas por columnas.

solution:
def patch_count(height, width, p):
    return -(-height // p) * -(-width // p)
